svg.title: Aegis Shield: a magnetic bubble against the solar wind
svg.desc: Along the Sun-Venus line, the bubble, the coil and Venus to scale, the distance not. The solar wind, 13.5 per cm³ at 400 km/s, flows round a magnetic bubble whose nose is 10,000 km from the coil, where the field of 95 nT balances the wind's 3.6 × 10⁻⁹ Pa. The coil, 1,000 km in radius, sits beside the Veil, 1.11 × 10⁶ km from Venus; at least 2.0 × 10¹¹ kg of carbon fibre holds it against its own field. Whether the sheltered region reaches Venus is an open question.
